name: Dwarves
label: Sub Pop
lede: The Dwarves played fifteen-minute sets, sent a masked guitarist onstage in studded leather underpants, and put out a press release announcing his murder. Sub Pop dropped them over it, and they're still going.

eras.title: A garage band built on community service
eras.text: Before the Dwarves there was Suburban Nightmare, a band of Chicago suburban kids who loved the Sonics and sixties punk. The new name, and the bad reputation, came in the mid-eighties.

years.h: Community service in suburban Chicago turns up a guitarist
years.p: After a drug bust, [[Blag Dahlia|2b47abbb-b6d8-4d0c-b989-b02fc649a5e0]] told SPIN, he met guitarist [[HeWhoCannotBeNamed|b9afc39f-05e4-4cc6-8373-b45ab0c4bada]] while both were doing community service. They start the garage band Suburban Nightmare.
years.xp: The band stayed Suburban Nightmare until Dahlia took over as frontman, when it became the Dwarves, per SPIN. Beat dates the change to the early eighties.

years.h: Suburban Nightmare's A Hard Day's Nightmare on Midnight Records
years.p: The pre-Dwarves band's LP of Sonics-style garage rock, later collected with other early tracks on Recess Records' Lick It.

years.h: Horror Stories: the first Dwarves album, on Voxx
years.p: Still garage and psychedelia, not yet hardcore. Blag Dahlia has taken over as frontman.

eras.title: Fifteen minutes, then blood
eras.text: In San Francisco the Dwarves sped up and got meaner, and became the American punk act people talked about most for the wrong reasons: self-mutilation, sex onstage, hard drugs, sets over in a quarter of an hour. Sub Pop signed them anyway.

years.p: Now in San Francisco, the Dwarves swap garage for fast, ugly hardcore on Nasty Gash Records, with [[GG Allin|0c624637-4a2c-4df0-ba80-b4ddb25bb5e5]] a clear model. The Lucifer's Crank EP follows.

years.cap: Blag Dahlia singing at a club show
yt: Full set at the Vogue, Seattle, Jan. 22, 1990
years.h: In a Dwarves set, fifteen minutes is plenty
years.p: Wikipedia describes early shows as self-mutilation, onstage sex and hard drugs, often wrapped up in a quarter of an hour. HeWhoCannotBeNamed played in a mask and studded leather underpants.

years.cap: Four Dwarves under the Times Square Adult Shop sign, New York
years.h: Sub Pop releases Blood Guts & Pussy: ten songs, 13 minutes
years.p: The cover shows two women and a blood-smeared dwarf actor, Bobby Faust. Riot grrrl figures including [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] criticized it.
years.xp:
The band got to Sub Pop by playing shows with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]], Dahlia told SPIN.

Dahlia has defended the cover as an art photo rather than cheesecake, he told Beat.

eras.title: Sub Pop's problem children
eras.text: Two more Sub Pop records turned the Dwarves into a cult band with real songs under the noise. The stunts kept escalating, and the last one cost them the label.

years.h: Hooks arrive on Thank Heaven for Little Girls
years.p: The second Sub Pop album keeps the short blasts but adds tunes, the start of the Dwarves as a songwriting band.

q: Half way through the show I realise everyone's looking to my right
years.h: A CMJ showcase, and HeWhoCannotBeNamed is up on the speaker stack
years.p: Mid-set he urinated off it, Blag Dahlia told Beat. The Dwarves had just signed to Sub Pop.

years.cap: Blag Dahlia in the crowd at a club show
years.h: A fan rakes a razor across Blag Dahlia's neck in Canada
years.p: It missed the jugular by about half an inch, Dahlia told SPIN. He finished the set bleeding.
years.xp: Dahlia said he had smashed the beer in the man's hand before the fan rushed the stage. "I was bleeding all over myself, I thought it looked cool," he told SPIN. A doctor later warned him he could have died.

years.h: The Dwarves announce HeWhoCannotBeNamed's murder, and Sub Pop drops them
years.p: Before Sugarfix, a press release said HeWho had been stabbed to death in Philadelphia. When Sub Pop learned it was a hoax, the label let the Dwarves go.
years.xp:
Asked about it by Beat, Dahlia said HeWho "transcends life and death so it's impossible to know when he was born or died."

Dahlia told SPIN Sub Pop knew in advance: "Instead of embracing the hoax like they did when we all came up with it, they turned their back on us." SPIN says Sub Pop has long denied that and declined to comment for the piece.

Sugarfix came out with a tribute to the supposedly dead guitarist. HeWho was alive and back in the band when it returned.

years.p: The third and final Sub Pop album. The split led to a hiatus of several years.

eras.title: The comeback, and a beer-soaked punch
eras.text: The Dwarves returned with Nick Oliveri, later of Queens of the Stone Age, on bass and a record that sounded like a band. They moved to Epitaph, landed a Jim Carrey movie, and ended up in a feud that reached court.

years.h: Back from the hiatus with The Dwarves Are Young and Good Looking
years.p: AllMusic's reviewer heard a new Dwarves that played real songs and left the club unbloodied. Nick Oliveri plays bass as Rex Everything.

years.h: Half a song into a label showcase, the Dwarves go through the drum kit
years.p: Given the showcase, they played half a song and then smashed their equipment, Dahlia told SPIN.
years.xp:
SPIN places it at an Epitaph showcase, after [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] signed them. Dahlia's account: "We played half of one song, jumped into the drum set, trashed everything, laughed, and walked off stage."

"The people from the label got very insulted," he added.

years.p: [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]]'s label puts out the next record, with a cover that nods to Blood Guts & Pussy.

years.h: Jim Carrey sings along to a Dwarves track in Me, Myself & Irene
years.p: The Farrelly brothers' comedy uses a Dwarves song; Wikipedia reports Dahlia was paid tens of thousands of dollars.
years.xp: The film's team first asked about one particular song. Dahlia realized he owned the compositions but not the Sub Pop-era masters, so he re-recorded the old hits for licensing on the 2001 album How to Win Friends and Influence People.

years.h: Josh Homme pours beer on Blag Dahlia, then hits him, at the Dragonfly
years.p: [[Josh Homme|dbecd515-aac9-4e7b-808e-bca22809c316]] hit Dahlia on the head before a Dwarves show in Los Angeles, a wound that needed stitches. The two had fallen out over Nick Oliveri, who played in both bands.
years.xp:
Homme pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor battery counts and got probation, per Rolling Stone.

That same year The Dwarves Must Die came out with guests including Oliveri, [[Dexter Holland|dbdf3e41-1978-49ba-8e23-2d09fe15347a]] of the Offspring and [[Nash Kato|df8e03a1-895f-4223-a50a-e4db58e99404]] of [[Urge Overkill|120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde]].

eras.title: Fifth decade, own label
eras.text: The Dwarves kept making records into their fifth decade, first on Burger Records and then, after Burger collapsed in 2020, on their own Greedy label.

years.cap: Blag Dahlia at the mic, live in Berlin
years.h: Burger Records signs the Dwarves for Take Back the Night
years.p: The California garage label collapses two years later amid misconduct allegations.

years.h: Vadge Moore writes it all down
years.p: Longtime drummer Vadge Moore's memoir My Life with the Dwarves covers drinking, fighting and sex on the road.

years.h: The Dwarves' own Greedy label puts out Jenkem
years.p: It follows Concept Album (2023) and Keep It Reel (2024). The lineup is Dahlia, HeWhoCannotBeNamed, Rex Everything, the Fresh Prince of Darkness and drummer Snupac.
